text.text: Plan every application, keep every deadline and never miss a report. Start with the Dashboard each Monday. Work the Overdue and Mine views, then check what is due in the next 7 days. When a grant is awarded, add its reports straight away so the dates are never lost.

Where it comes from
What to do about it
Awarded (USD)
Sum of awarded amounts on that funder's grants marked Awarded
Compare with the year's target on the first of each month
Reports still owed
Reports for the grant not yet submitted
Add every report when the award letter arrives
Asked, still open (USD)
Amounts asked on grants still being drafted or submitted
Use it to forecast the year, but count only awards as money

text.text: Funders reject careless applications faster than weak ideas. This checklist keeps the basics from sinking a good proposal.
Before writing
Read the guidelines twice and note page limits
Confirm eligibility and the geographic area
Call the program officer if anything is unclear
Put the due date and two internal deadlines on the calendar
Writing
State the need with one number a stranger would remember
Describe what will change and how you will know
Match the budget lines to the narrative
Ask a colleague outside the program to read it cold
Before submitting
Attach every document asked for, with the requested file names
Check the portal limit on characters and file size
Submit one day early
Press Mark submitted and add the decision date
A grant is only finished when the final report is accepted. The funder remembers late reports at renewal time.
The day the award arrives
Press Mark awarded and enter the amount and the grant period dates.
Read the agreement and list every report with its due date in the Reports table.
Tell the program director what the money must be spent on, in plain words.
Each reporting period
Collect numbers monthly so the report is a summary, not a research project.
Keep two stories and two photos with permission on file.
Send the draft to finance two weeks before the due date.
If something changes
If a program changes or money cannot be spent as planned, email the program officer before the change, not after. Note the answer on the grant row.
The best use of a grant writer's time is a short list of funders who already care about your work.
